clue.text: Bit of an exercise, instruction to lift operator?

definitions.meaning: one push-up repetition within a workout routine
a lift is a British elevator, so its attendant might be told which button to hit to go higher

explanation.definitionFit: A single push-up in a workout is called this, and the phrase also reads as an order to an elevator attendant to ascend.

clue.text: 13 bread-maker on reservation, quite possibly? That's false!

indicators.note: the cross-reference points to the clue whose answer means spoken, so the words that follow are to be said out loud

parts.note: dough makes bread, and the Sioux are a Native American people associated with reservations, so this is Sioux dough

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a Native American baker, met with an indignant cry of falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: The '13' reference stands for 'pronounced': say SIOUX DOUGH and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix-like adjective means sham or not genuine, a direct synonym of false.

clue.text: It doesn't matter which here, it turns out

indicators.note: the phrase suggests the letters of the preceding words emerge in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that any choice will do, as things turn out here.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of two options, the word means one or the other, whichever you like, so it does not matter which.

clue.text: Fish and snake on the road, one sliding down the street?

parts.note: a skate is a flat sea fish
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A fish and a snake out on the road, one of them slipping down the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled board ridden by someone gliding along pavements, described playfully as a slider down the street.

clue.text: 13 two girls, one required by the Grauniad?

indicators.note: the cross-reference stands for spoken, so the girls' names are to be said out loud

parts.note: Pru and Freda are two girls' names

explanation.surface: Two young women apparently needed by a newspaper nicknamed for its typos.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is mocked as the Grauniad for its misprints, so it needs someone checking copy; say PRU FREDA to hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A checker of printed copy for errors, ironically what a typo-ridden paper most needs.

clue.text: Hard, Proust, funny old comic

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the novelist's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of a hard-going French novelist and an old humorous magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges the novelist's name. Hotspur was a British boys' story paper, later a comic, that ran from 1933 to 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British boys' periodical of the twentieth century, hence a comic from the past.

clue.text: Southern African's sexy figure, baby!

parts.note: hot means sexy or attractive
ten is a number, a figure
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone from southern Africa is admired as having an attractive figure, with 'baby!' tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is a dated name for the Khoikhoi people of south-western Africa, now regarded as offensive.

clue.text: 13 drop down the face, piece of cake?

indicators.note: the cross-reference stands for spoken, so the phrase that follows is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tear is a drop of water running down the cheek

explanation.surface: A tear rolls down someone's cheek over a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' tempts as 'easy', but it means a layer of a wedding cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of a stacked celebration cake is called this, so it is literally a piece of one.

clue.text: 13 fish, orangey-red for some pastry

indicators.note: the cross-reference stands for spoken, so the two words are to be heard run together

parts.note: a pike is a freshwater fish and rust is an orangey-red colour

explanation.surface: A fish and a reddish colour somehow end up as pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Say PIKE RUST quickly and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The baked shell or lid of a pie is a kind of pastry.

clue.text: 13, studied and criticised a Chinese mammal

indicators.note: the cross-reference stands for spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: read (said 'red') means studied, panned means criticised, and then 'a'

explanation.surface: A reviewer examined and slated something, which turns out to be an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' here is past tense, said like 'red'; READ PANNED A sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reddish tree-dwelling mammal of China and the Himalayas.

clue.text: Further Essex traffic jams

indicators.note: jams here means squeezes in or holds, so the words grip the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A complaint about the extra gridlock on Essex roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional, beyond what is usual, is a synonym of further.

clue.text: One-on-one combat taken outside that is, character this pumped in the tank?

indicators.note: the fight goes round the other pieces, as if the combatants step outside

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two people
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
self means one's character or identity

explanation.surface: Two people fight outside a pub, and someone wonders about what goes into a vehicle tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken outside' means the fight word goes around the other two pieces; the definition is a cryptic hint at a filling-station pump, with 'tank' a fuel tank rather than an army one.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil-derived fuel that a filling station pumps into a vehicle's tank.

clue.text: 24 a 24 — on the contrary

indicators.note: contrary means the opposite way, so the tune word is read backwards

parts.note: the second cross-reference to 24 means song, and air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced riddle about one song and another, said contrarily.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo vocal piece in opera, a kind of song.

clue.text: It's said to be obvious

definitions.meaning: uttered or spoken, as a word is with a particular sound
marked or very noticeable, as in a strong accent

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both articulated in speech and very noticeable, as of a limp or an accent.

clue.text: Posh tea (unfinished) included sandwiches produced by machines?

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: comprised means included or contained
U is the label for upper-class, posh usage

indicators.note: the drink word loses its last letter, left incomplete

parts.note: the drink as written

explanation.surface: A posh tea, left half eaten, with sandwiches apparently made by machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last letter off the drink, and 'sandwiches' puts the posh letter and the cut drink inside the word for included. U is the crossword shorthand for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handled by computers is automated, made or done by machines.

clue.text: Promote correct manner of ambulation, as 13

indicators.note: the cross-reference means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: proper means correct, and gait is a manner of walking

explanation.surface: Advocating the right way to walk, said in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: PROPER GAIT said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread or publicise an idea is to promote it.

clue.text: Iodine thus something to discuss regarding similar elementary forms

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
so means thus or in this way
a topic is a subject for discussion

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about iodine and a discussion topic on related elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms of the same element with differing neutron counts are related forms of an element, hence the adjective.

clue.text: Potential layer in this painting finish?

definitions.meaning: a laying hen develops inside an egg before it hatches
a paint finish with a slight sheen, between matt and gloss

explanation.definitionFit: A future hen grows within the egg's casing, and decorators use the same name for a low-sheen paint.

clue.text: Making sweet love in windy act, ruing gas

indicators.note: the zero letter goes inside the rearranged letters
windy suggests blown about, so the letters of the three words are scattered

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance in a gassy performance, regretting the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' scrambles the three words, and 'in' puts the tennis zero among them. 'Making sweet' is the definition, not 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating with sugar makes food sweet, and figuratively makes bad news pleasanter.

clue.text: Weak character from outer space, a Klingon, as 13?

parts.note: limp means weak or floppy
ET is the alien in the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A feeble alien, a Star Trek Klingon perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'a Klingon' and you hear 'a cling-on': the shellfish clings to rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish fastens itself tightly to rocks, so it is something that clings on.

clue.text: See 4
Hitler had a little one — thanks mum!

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
mum means keep quiet, as does sh

explanation.surface: A joke about the dictator's small moustache, ending with a thank you to mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum here is not mother: 'keep mum' means stay silent, hence SH. The surface echoes a rude British wartime song.
explanation.definitionFit: The dictator wore a small toothbrush moustache, and this is short British slang for one.

clue.text: Former ANC president, wee thing shaken

parts.note: Oliver Tambo led the African National Congress
wee is informal British for urine

explanation.surface: A former South African leader and a small thing shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like small, but it is the noun for pee.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument with jingles in its frame, played by being shaken.

clue.text: Something cheeky about capital of Rhodesia, a nation now renamed

indicators.note: the bottom word goes around the initial letter

parts.note: bum is British slang for bottom, the seat of the cheeks

indicators.note: capital means the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something cheeky going on around Rhodesia's capital, a country that later changed its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-east Asian country is now officially called Myanmar, so its old name is outdated.

clue.text: Number of prison gates

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is formed from part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The number of the prison's gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a count but a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical number is a piece performed in a show, here a sung piece.

clue.text: Flying reptile, frightening thing with lots of teeth, as 13?

indicators.note: the cross-reference means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: frightening thing with lots of teeth
parts.note: terror is a frightening thing and a saw has lots of teeth

explanation.surface: A winged reptile described as a frightening creature with many teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent: TERROR SAW said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct winged reptile of the dinosaur age.

clue.text: Archer prize idiot, discard one and many books

parts.note: a cup is a trophy, a prize

indicators.note: discard means throw away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the word as written
I is the Roman numeral one
OT, the Old Testament, contains many books

explanation.surface: A prize fool ditching a single item and a load of books.
explanation.walkthrough: From IDIOT, discard I and OT to leave ID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is portrayed with a bow and arrows, hence an archer.

clue.text: Scent block in the shape of roadworks?

indicators.note: the wooden block goes inside the traffic marker

parts.note: roadworks are marked off with traffic cones
a log is a block of wood

explanation.surface: A whiff from a block cut to resemble roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de toilette is a light perfume, a scent.

clue.text: Christian hoarding treasure primarily after gold, as money expert

indicators.note: the fashion name comes after the gold symbol

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: hoarding means holding a stash, so the designer's name contains the letter

parts.note: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fashion designer stockpiling riches, chasing gold like a financial expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who inspects financial records is an expert in money matters.
